newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound continues rise on dlr oversupply.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound continues rise on dlr oversupply.

text.p: Dollars were in oversupply on the Beirut foreign exchange market in the week ended on Friday as the Lebanese pound continued its steady appreciation against the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The central bank lowered its intervention rate to 1,546.50-1,557 pounds to the dollar on Friday from 1,547-1,557 where it had stood since last Friday.

The pound has continued its steady, four-year appreciation against the dollar since the central bank shifted its intervention mechanism in September from a single mid-price quotation to a bid-offer system, effectively creating an inter-bank market.

Much of the activity at present comprises sales of dollars by people seeking to buy government treasury bills denominated in Lebanese pounds which carry annual interest rates of 14.27 to 19.28 percent.
Dealers said the inter-bank market was quiet during the week and commercial banks absorbed only a fraction of the dollars on offer.

Talal Abou Zaki, foreign exchange manager at Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, said inter-bank trade was restricted to a very narrow band of 10 or 20 piastres at the bottom end of the intervention band.
"Inter-bank trading today was 1,546.5-1,546.6 or 1,546.7," Abou Zaki said. "Commercial banks don't need dollars. They could buy as many as they want."
He estimated that commercial banks bought about 10 percent of the dollars on offer and the central bank absorbed the rest.
